highlighted_projects.description: Researched and implemented an IoT-based system using Raspberry Pi and RFID scanners to monitor passenger counts on National University of Singapore (NUS) campus buses. Collected and analyzed data from RFID inputs to determine bus occupancy trends, enabling data-driven recommendations for optimizing the number of buses deployed on specific routes. Integrated GPS data and weather information to study external factors affecting travel time and schedule disruptions. The insights supported more efficient route planning and resource allocation within the campus transport system.
highlighted_projects.name: Smart Buss App

jarvis_projects.description: The Linux Cluster Monitoring Agent is a Bash-scripted MVP designed to help the Linux Cluster Administration team at Jarvis automate server monitoring. It collects hardware specs and real-time resource usage data from Linux nodes, storing it in a PostgreSQL database running in a Docker container. Scripts (host_info.sh and host_usage.sh) capture static and dynamic data, respectively, with host_usage.sh running every minute via crontab. The system supports automated data logging, centralized storage, and performance analysis, significantly reducing manual monitoring. Git and Docker were used for version control and containerized deployment, ensuring portability and maintainability.
jarvis_projects.name: Linux  Cluster Monitor Project

jarvis_projects.description: A SQL-based project designed to manage a country club's data, including members, facilities, and booking history. The system supports core database operations such as inserting records, removing members, updating facility costs, analyzing monthly bookings, and identifying popular facilities.
jarvis_projects.name: RDBMS_SQL Project

jarvis_projects.description: A hands-on project focused on requirements gathering, system analysis, and documentation. I developed a Business Requirements Document (BRD) for a Linux Cluster Monitoring Agent, outlining business needs, technical specifications, and implementation strategy using PostgreSQL, Docker, and Bash scripting. Additionally, I created a System Requirements Document (SRD) for a mobile-first Retail Investor Stock Trading Application, detailing functional and non-functional requirements, user needs, and compliance standards. This project strengthened my skills in stakeholder communication, Agile methodology, SQL, and end-to-end documentation aligned with industry practices.
jarvis_projects.name: BSA Project

jarvis_projects.description: Developed a data analytics pipeline for the London Gift Shop (LGS) using Python, Jupyter Notebook, and PostgreSQL. The project ingested and transformed a historical SQL retail dataset into actionable insights. Implemented RFM segmentation, customer acquisition analysis, and sales trend visualizations. Utilized Pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib for data wrangling and plotting. PostgreSQL ran inside a Docker container simulating an OLAP environment, and Git was used for version control. The solution supports data-driven decision-making in marketing and operations.
jarvis_projects.name: Python Data Analytics Project

jarvis_projects.description: In this Power BI project, three distinct dashboards were developed to address different analytical needs. The Beverage Dashboard offers detailed insights into beverage sales performance, including trends over time, top products, and customer segmentation, supporting marketing and inventory decisions. The Data Professionals Survey Report visualizes responses from a 2022 survey of over 600 data professionals, highlighting career roles, job satisfaction, demographics, and industry trends to inform workforce analytics. Finally, the Stocks Dashboard integrates live stock data via the Alpha Vantage API, providing comprehensive views of daily stock prices, trading volume, key financial ratios, and earnings estimates, with dynamic filtering options to assist in investment analysis.
jarvis_projects.name: Power BI Dashboard Project

jarvis_projects.description: Implemented a scalable Hadoop cluster on Google Cloud Platform (1 master, 2 worker nodes) to evaluate Hadoop as an alternative to legacy analytics tools like SAP and R. Designed and validated distributed storage and processing workflows using HDFS, YARN, and Hive, with interactive exploration in Zeppelin notebooks. Performed benchmarking on a 1TB stock trades dataset, reducing execution times from hours to minutes through distributed computing. Optimized Hive queries with year-based partitioning, Parquet storage (shrinking data from 1.7 GB to 263 MB), and the Tez execution engine, achieving up to 45x faster query performance. Explored MapReduce, Tez, and HiveQL to compare imperative vs. declarative SQL approaches in large-scale analytics.
jarvis_projects.name: Hadoop Big Data Analytics Project
